title: Pauri 27, meaning: the house where all sing
hook: what is that door where you sit and care for all? Wind, water, fire and countless beings sing there (Japji 27)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the question at the door. Your line was so dar: what is that door, what is that house? Did a doorway bring the question with it? Today, we listen in. Day two hundred eight.

Sit outside at dawn some morning and just listen. First it seems quiet. Then you notice the birds, dozens of them, each with its own tune. Wind moving through a tree. Water somewhere, a gutter, a sprinkler. A far-off truck, a dog, a door. After a few minutes it doesn't sound like noise anymore. It sounds like an orchestra tuning up. Pauri 27 asked what that door is like, where the One sits and cares for all. Its answer isn't a description of a building. It's a sound.
screen: `OUTSIDE AT DAWN.` → `BIRDS, WIND, WATER, A DOG.` → `AN ORCHESTRA TUNING UP.`

segments.voice: What is that door, that house, where You sit and care for all? Pauri 27 answers with music, in paraphrase. There, countless instruments play, and countless are the players. So many ragas, the melodies of Indian music, and so many singers. Then who's singing? The elements first. In the original: gaavahi tuhano paun paanee baisantar. Wind, water and fire sing to You. Then, in paraphrase: the king of dharma sings at Your door, and the recorders who write down every deed. Shiva, Brahma and the goddess sing. Indra sings, among the gods. The siddhas, the celibates, the truthful, the contented, the brave warriors sing. The pandits and the sages with their Vedas, age after age. The continents and worlds and universes sing. Those who please You sing, Your devotees, steeped in Your love. And so many others sing that I can't even think of them all, Nanak says. Look at that list. Wind and fire. Gods of every name people knew in Guru Nanak's world. Scholars and warriors. Whole galaxies. Every one of them is singing to the same One. Nobody is outside the choir. Then the stanza settles, in paraphrase: He is, He is, forever true, the true Master, true His Name. He is, and will be, and won't pass away. Whatever pleases Him, He does; no one can give Him orders. He is the King, the King of kings, and Nanak says: live within His will. So the door from yesterday opens onto a sound. And the stanza invites you to hear your own ordinary morning as part of it.
screen: `COUNTLESS INSTRUMENTS AND PLAYERS.` · `WIND, WATER AND FIRE SING.` · `GODS, SAGES, WORLDS, DEVOTEES.` · `HE IS, HE IS, FOREVER TRUE.` · then, large: `EVERYTHING IS SINGING.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and listen to whatever is around you: traffic, a fan, your own breath, a voice in another room. Instead of sorting sounds into good and bad, try hearing all of them as singing, each one its own voice in the choir. The hum of the fridge. The breath in your nose. Let nothing be noise for these two minutes. The bell holds the time.
Pauri 27. At that door, countless instruments play; wind, water and fire, gods, sages and whole worlds sing. He is, forever true.
Your line: everything is singing. Today, when a sound annoys you, a horn, an alarm, a crying child, try once to hear it as one more voice in the choir. Day two hundred eight.

howItsDone: Pauri 27 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib, and a version of it is sung in the evening as So Dar in Rehras Sahib; in gurdwaras, kirtan, sung praise with instruments, echoes its picture of the whole creation singing.

options: countless beings, elements and worlds, all singing.
a single judge on a throne.
fork.reveal: countless instruments, countless singers: wind, water, fire, gods, sages, worlds and devotees, all singing to the One.

original.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 27: wind, water and fire sing to You.

trapdoor: what you thought: heaven is a place with a door.
what it means: the answer to where the One sits is a sound: all creation singing.
what a scholar hears: the stanza names Dharamraj, Chitragupt, Shiva, Brahma, Devi and Indra among the singers, then turns to so ee so ee, He is, He is, and ends in rajaa'ee, the divine will.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 6 (Japji, Pauri 27, the singers and the closing lines)

notes: The list of singers is abridged (e.g., the enchanting beauties, the 68 pilgrimage places, the four sources of creation are left out); confirm.
'kete raag paree siu kaheean' paraphrased as 'so many ragas'; the raginis (consorts) are not named. Confirm.
Trapdoor floor 3 transliterates rajaa'ee informally; confirm.
